item.research_question: What are the magnetic properties of the high-entropy alloy FeCoNiTi?
item.material_system: FeCoNiTi, a high-entropy alloy with a dual phase comprising face-centered cubic (fcc) and hexagonal C14 Laves phases
item.processing_route: The as-cast polycrystalline sample was prepared through a homemade arc furnace, with the elemental components remelted several times and rapidly quenched on a water-cooled Cu hearth
item.test_conditions: Temperature-dependent DC magnetization χdc (T) ranging from 50 to 400 K, and isothermal magnetization (M) curves at various temperatures
key_findings: The HEA manifests three distinct ferromagnetic orderings at 1084, 214, and 168 K
The emergence of the 214 K transition is attributed to the influence of the C14 phase
The high-temperature ordering at 1084 K is associated with the fcc phase, which exhibits an additional ferromagnetic ordering at 168 K
The coercive field of the fcc phase attains 667 Oe at 400 K
Electronic structure calculations substantiate the presence of ferromagnetic ground states in both phases
The Ms values at 50 K for both phases closely align with the theoretical magnetic moments
item.mechanism: The magnetic properties of the fcc and C14 phases are attributed to the ferromagnetic ground states, with the C14 phase inducing the ferromagnetic ordering at 214 K and the fcc phase inducing the remaining two orderings
quotes: The HEA manifests three distinct ferromagnetic orderings at 1084, 214, and 168 K
The coercive field of the fcc phase attains 667 Oe at 400 K
The Ms values at 50 K for both phases closely align with the theoretical magnetic moments

records.text: Paper card. Question: What are the magnetic properties of the high-entropy alloy FeCoNiTi?. System: FeCoNiTi, a high-entropy alloy with a dual phase comprising face-centered cubic (fcc) and hexagonal C14 Laves phases. Processing: The as-cast polycrystalline sample was prepared through a homemade arc furnace, with the elemental components remelted several times and rapidly quenched on a water-cooled Cu hearth. Test conditions: Temperature-dependent DC magnetization χdc (T) ranging from 50 to 400 K, and isothermal magnetization (M) curves at various temperatures. Findings: The HEA manifests three distinct ferromagnetic orderings at 1084, 214, and 168 K; The emergence of the 214 K transition is attributed to the influence of the C14 phase; The high-temperature ordering at 1084 K is associated with the fcc phase, which exhibits an additional ferromagnetic ordering at 168 K; The coercive field of the fcc phase attains 667 Oe at 400 K; Electronic structure calculations substantiate the presence of ferromagnetic ground states in both phases; The Ms values at 50 K for both phases closely align with the theoretical magnetic moments. Mechanism: The magnetic properties of the fcc and C14 phases are attributed to the ferromagnetic ground states, with the C14 phase inducing the ferromagnetic ordering at 214 K and the fcc phase inducing the remaining two orderings. Quote: "The HEA manifests three distinct ferromagnetic orderings at 1084, 214, and 168 K"
